result.title: Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization
result.summary: Self-distillation policy optimization provides dense token-level supervision for LLM post-training through feedback-conditioned self-teachers. However, directly matching the self-teacher can disrupt successful behaviors on correct rollouts while providing insufficient correction on incorrect ones. We propose Asymmetric Policy Optimization via Self-Distillation (APSD), which constructs correctness-dependent targets by mixing student and self-teacher distributions: interpolation preserves successful behaviors on correct rollouts, while extrapolation beyond the self-teacher strengthens correction on incorrect ones. We analyze APSD through divergence decomposition, reverse-KL barycentric geometry, and gradient analysis, highlighting the importance of gradient flow through student-dependent targets. Experiments under reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards and rich feedback show that APSD achieves strong overall performance against reinforcement-learning and self-distillation baselines and matches SDPO performance with 2.6x fewer training steps on average across Qwen3 model scales.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 APSD，以正确性为条件混合学生与自教师分布（正确轨迹做插值保留、错误轨迹做外推加强纠正），并通过散度分解、reverse-KL 重心几何与梯度分析说明学生相关目标中梯度流的作用，在带可验证奖励与丰富反馈的 RL 设定下评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本策略优化工作，不含视觉或显式 latent 推理；但其按正确性构造目标分布、以及"目标依赖学生状态时梯度流才有效"的分析，可能为 LVR 的轨迹监督与贡献分配提供线索，是否可迁移需核查。
